cases.purpose: Verify tee -i restores the caller's trapped and ignored SIGINT dispositions, and a normal tee invocation does not leak its immediate-interrupt state into later shell commands.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils tee under the same Bash shell
cases.comparison: Byte parity and status; self-signals target only the fixture shell after tee has returned. A trapped signal must execute its trap, and an ignored signal must leave the shell running.
cases.script:
trap 'printf "trap-ran\n"' INT
tee -i </dev/null >/dev/null
printf 'ignore-status=%d\n' "$?"
kill -INT "$$"
printf 'after-trap\n'
tee </dev/null >/dev/null
printf 'plain-status=%d\n' "$?"
kill -INT "$$"
printf 'after-plain-trap\n'
trap '' INT
tee -i </dev/null >/dev/null
kill -INT "$$"
printf 'after-ignored\n'
